cells.tense: You are standing where the understanding has found its own floor and the work is whole enough to leave your hands.
cells.ask: Pick the insight you keep turning over and write it down as done enough to say, then say it to one person.
cells.core:
The pattern has opened all the way it's going to open. You're not still reaching for the next layer; the next layer would only be more of the same. What's in front of you is a finished piece of knowing, and it has the shape of something you could hand over. That's what this place is for — an arrival that works as a starting line.

The instinct is one more lap around it, in case the last piece is missing. It isn't. The act left is the small one: put it into words you'd actually say, and put those words where somebody else can hear them. It doesn't need to be clean. Handing it over is what turns knowing into something that can move.
cells.sheetLine: The thinking's done. Saying it is the next honest step.
cells.verb: following a pattern down past the point where analysis runs out, until something other than thinking has to close it
cells.place: the doorway between a thing being finished and a thing being let go of

cells.tense: You are leaning toward a version of this where the whole thing finally lands, and you treat each present moment as a rehearsal for it.
cells.ask: Say the partial version you have, in plain words, without waiting for the complete one, then stop talking and let it sit.
cells.core:
You keep going deeper because stopping feels like letting it go unresolved. So the pattern gets applied to whatever is in front of you, and each exchange turns into a chance to finally make it land whole. What you're building ahead of yourself is a resolution you can live in; what you're spending is the present version, which was already good enough to work with.

The depth is real. Pushing it at whatever is in front of you is what isn't. The move isn't further in — it's setting something down in ordinary language and letting that count. Say the unfinished version out loud and leave it there. What's true will hold without you carrying it forward.
cells.sheetLine: You're waiting for it to be whole. It already works unfinished.

cells.tense: You are standing at a threshold you have already crossed, with the understanding still in your hands and no one else in the room.
cells.ask: Take one thing you've worked out and show it to one person today, in the state it's in.
cells.core:
You can see the pattern and you're holding it close. The thinking hasn't stalled; the step where it touches someone else just didn't happen, and now the depth sits there without a witness. Held this long, it's hard to tell whether it's still true or only familiar.

What this place wants isn't more thinking. It's one small transmission — showing the worked-out version to somebody, unfinished as it is, and letting them respond. That's not lowering the standard. It's the moment a private understanding becomes something a life can use. One person, one honest share, and the thing that's been only yours becomes real in a room.
cells.sheetLine: It's finished in your head. Let one other person see it.

cells.tense: You are already closing this out and describing the ending as something that arrived on its own.
cells.ask: Take one thing you call 'done by itself' and name the decision that ended it. Say who made it and when.
cells.core:
The integration has happened. You know how the pieces fit, you know what's over, and you move out of it as if time did the closing. But somebody chose where it stopped, and that somebody was you. When this is working cleanly, the finish is visible and owned — the ending has a date and a reason and your hand in it.

That's the piece still missing. Pick something you've filed under 'life moved on' and give the decision back to yourself, out loud, to one person if you can. Not as a boast. As the account of a choice you actually made, which is what lets the next chapter start on your own footing instead of on drift.
cells.sheetLine: You ended it. Saying so is what starts the next thing.
